description: Reference choreography from the @121.sincere TikTok (11.3 s of dancing before the TikTok end card). Solo dancer in a parking lot, full body, hand-held rear camera that pushes in around 4.3-5.0 s. Move boundaries from the wrist/elbow/knee/ankle trajectories and motion energy of data/dance/pose/121sincere_ccea87.npz (see docs/DANCE_MODEL_INTERFACE.md section 4 for the schema).
bpm_estimate_note: Estimated from the pose data only (no audio): the left wrist pumps once per beat over 5.3-11.3 s (spectral peak 2.04 Hz) and the right-wrist pattern repeats every 4 beats (autocorrelation peak at 1.97 s), both giving 122 +/- 4 bpm.

moves.name: Ready pose: hands up gripping the hood at the sides of the head, still
Hands drop from the hood and sweep across the chest as the body turns side-on to the left
Side-on freeze: knees bent, left arm pushed forward with the palm open, hold
Turn back to face front, both arms shoot up into a W overhead while hopping on the left foot and swinging the right leg
Arms drop to the sides and the body bounces in a wide stance with a forward lean
Arms open out wide to both sides with a side lean, then the hands come in and cross at the chest
Alternating hand pumps at chest height on every beat, ending with the right index finger pointed up beside the head
Alternating hand pumps at chest height, finishing with both index fingers raised beside the head
Hands back to the chest and the arms cross, then both hands rise above the head to finish

notes: Dancing ends at the last ok frame 340 (11.33 s); frames 341-460 are the TikTok end card (ok=False), so the last move ends at 11.3 s.
All 17 joints are visible in 100% of ok frames (ankles included), so the 'legs' fault can fire on this dance; the legs only do something distinctive in arms_up_leg_swing and wide_bounce.
The camera pushes in between about 4.3 and 5.0 s (torso length in pixels grows ~30%): use hip-centred, torso-scaled coordinates rather than pixel positions.

'ready' is padded to the 0.8 s minimum move length: the hands actually start dropping from the hood at about 0.5 s, but count_in_s is 0.8 so that it equals the t0 of drop_sweep_turn, the first danced move.
Clip is not mirrored (filmed by another person with the rear camera): the dancer's right hand is on the image left. The single-finger point-ups at ~6.4, 7.7, 10.7 s are with the right hand.
'ready' is the count-in: the judge's reference clock starts count_in_s after the first ok learner frame unless set_ref_clock is used.
